questions.stem: What does System.out.println("VPN") do?

options.why: println writes the text and a newline.

questions.stem: A method trims the title, then rejects it when nothing remains. What happens to the input "   "?

options.why: After trim the text is empty, so the check rejects it.

options.text: It is stored as three spaces
options.why: The brief rejects a blank result after trim.
Untitled is not part of the check.
The input is not null, so trim itself is not a null failure.

questions.stem: Which check asks whether two strings have the same characters?

options.why: == asks whether they are the same object.
equals asks about the characters.
A single = assigns. It does not compare.
Printing does not compare.

questions.explanation: Use equals for character content. == is an object identity check.

questions.stem: A method declares int count; and then reads count before any assignment. What happens?

options.text: The compiler rejects the read of an unassigned local variable
options.why: Local variables have no compiler-supplied default.
That default applies to fields, not to this unread local.
int is not null.

options.text: The program prints count and continues
options.why: The compiler does not let this read through.

questions.explanation: The compiler never assigns a default to an uninitialized local variable.

questions.stem: A file contains public class Ticket. Which file name matches the public class?

Main.java does not match the public class Ticket.
The public class name and the file name must match.
A .class file is compiled output, not the source the tutorial asks you to save.

questions.stem: The method throws IllegalArgumentException for a blank title. Why is catch (Exception ex) a weak handler here?

options.text: It also catches unrelated failures and can hide them
options.why: Exception is a wide type. It hides failures the method did not mean to handle.
IllegalArgumentException is an Exception, so it is caught, and that is the problem.
The worked example does throw for a blank title.
catch is legal. The problem is the width.

questions.explanation: Catch IllegalArgumentException if that is the named failure. A catch of Exception is wider than the brief.

questions.stem: In this batch, what does a React component function do?

options.why: Saving is not this function's job.
React is not a Java compiler.

options.why: The parent still supplies props.

questions.stem: Where does a prop value come from?

options.text: The child invents it at render time
options.why: A missing prop should stay missing, not be invented.

options.text: The parent passes it in, and the child reads it
options.why: Props are inputs from the parent.
CSS does not pass the title.
The SQL sandbox is not the component parent.

questions.explanation: The parent passes the prop. The child reads it.

questions.stem: const [title, setTitle] = useState(""). What is title on the first render?

options.why: The argument was an empty string, not null.
Untitled was not passed to useState.
useState("") starts title as an empty string.
This state is local to the component. It is not another user's value.

styleClass is not the JSX attribute.

questions.stem: Which input is controlled by title state?

options.why: onChange alone does not display the state as the current value.
value and onChange together keep the field tied to state.
value without onChange does not write the next keystroke back through the setter in this pattern.
defaultValue does not keep the field controlled by title.

questions.stem: A list of tickets can be filtered. Which key identifies a row?

options.why: The index changes when the list is filtered or reordered.
ticket.id stays with that ticket.

options.text: The word key as the title
options.why: The word key is not an identity.
A CSS class does not identify the row.

questions.stem: A handler does tickets.push(row) and does not call the state setter. What does React do?

options.text: It is not asked to render the new list from state
options.why: The setter was not called, so React was not told to render the new list.

options.text: It saves the ticket on the server
options.why: push does not perform an HTTP create.
This line does not touch title.
push is an array method, not the setter.

questions.explanation: Mutating the array does not schedule the render. Call the setter with the next list.

questions.stem: title is "". The click handler calls setTitle("VPN") and then reads title on the next line. What does that read see?

options.why: The setter does not change title in the function that is already running.
The already executing code still sees the previous state.
The state was an empty string, not null.

options.text: The parent's prop, not the state variable
options.why: The read is the state variable, which has not updated yet.

questions.explanation: setTitle schedules the next render. The next line still sees the old title.

questions.stem: Why is title = "VPN" the wrong way to remember a new title in a function component?

options.text: It does not update state, so React does not re-render from that assignment
options.why: The local assignment does not tell React to store a new state value.
Assignment is not compilation.
This line is not an HTTP request.

options.text: It is the same operation as setTitle
options.why: setTitle is the state update. A plain assignment is not.

questions.explanation: Use the setter from useState. A plain assignment does not schedule a render from state.

questions.stem: In this batch's log, what is GET /tickets/1 used for?

options.why: GET on that path is the read in this log.
Create is the POST that returned 201.
No delete appears in the log.
The log is HTTP, not a Java compile.

questions.stem:
Using only this log, what does status 201 on row 2 mean?

| # | Method | Path | Body sent | Status | Body returned |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | GET | /tickets/1 | none | 200 | {"id": 1, "title": "Printer"} |
| 2 | POST | /tickets | {"title": "VPN"} | 201 | {"id": 4, "title": "VPN"} |
| 3 | GET | /tickets/9 | none | 404 | {"error": "not found"} |
| 4 | POST | /tickets | {} | 400 | {"error": "title is required"} |
| 5 | GET | /tickets/2 | none | 200 | {"id": 2, "title": "Laptop"} |
| 6 | GET | /tickets/3 | none | 500 | {"error": "server failed"} |

options.why: Not found is 404 on row 3.
Row 2 returned 201 and a ticket id.
A server failure is 500 on row 6.
A missing title is 400 on row 4.

questions.explanation: 201 on the POST means the ticket was created. It is not a failure just because it is not 200.

Using only this log, what does status 404 on row 3 mean?

questions.stem: The numbers 10, 20, and 30 are one set. What is their average?

options.why: That drops the 30.
30 is the largest value, not the average.
60 is the sum, not the average.

questions.stem: What is 15% of 200?

options.why: 15 is the percent, not the part of 200.
150 would be 75% of 200.
215 adds the percent to the base.

questions.explanation: 15% of 200 is 30. No further increase is stated.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours. Pipe B fills the same tank in 6 hours. How long do they take together, if both fill and neither leaks?

options.why: Adding the hours is not the combined rate.
18 is the product of the hours.
2 would be a faster rate than the two pipes together.

questions.explanation: Add the rates, not the hours. Together they fill one quarter of the tank per hour.

questions.stem: A fee of 400 increases by 10%. What is the increase, not the new fee?

options.why: 10 is the percent, not the money.
440 is the new fee.
360 subtracts the increase.

questions.explanation: The question asks for the increase. 10% of 400 is 40.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 8 hours. Pipe B empties the same tank in 24 hours. Both are open. How long does a full fill take from empty?

options.why: 6 would be a faster net rate than A alone minus B.
16 adds the hours in a way the rates do not support.
32 is slower than the empty rate alone.

questions.explanation: Subtract the emptying rate from the filling rate. The net rate fills the tank in 12 hours.

questions.stem: Which number is the odd one out: 2, 4, 8, 9, 16?

options.why: 2 is a power of 2.
4 is a power of 2.

16 is a power of 2.

questions.stem: Ravi is Meera's brother. Meera is Ali's mother. Which relation must hold?

The sentences do not make Ravi the father.
Ali is the child, not Ravi's mother.
Meera is the mother, not the brother.

questions.explanation: Use only the two sentences. Ravi is the mother's brother.

before matches the ordinary meaning: required beforehand.
instead of replaces the next step.
